key_insight: Compressing each matrix optimally is not enough; the best low-rank LLM compression comes from a three-level optimization chain that refines from per-matrix SVD to block-level joint tuning and then end-to-end loss minimization.
engineering_relevance: For practical LLM deployment, the paper shows that structured multi-stage optimization can deliver much lower perplexity at high compression than independent matrix truncation, even with only 256 calibration sequences.
method: L1: whitened SVD truncation for individual matrices
L2: joint optimization over each Transformer block
L3: end-to-end language-modeling loss refinement on the full model
evidence_signal: On LLaMA-7B at 60% compression, WikiText-2 perplexity improved from 42.1 to 19.1 to 11.4 across the three stages, with gains reported across 20–80% compression, five architectures, and in-/out-of-distribution benchmarks.
watch_item: The block-level stage is important but compute/data trade-offs matter; skipping it can be competitive only when more calibration data is available, and the reported downstream task accuracy remains below the dense model.
paper_title: Per-Matrix Optimality Is Not Enough: Three-Level Optimization for Low-Rank LLM Compression
